# Neutral luminance and alpha conversion

Original OPC/XML controls generated by `tools/picture_luminance_neutral_fixture.py`
using the repository's authored color strip. No corpus content is included.
Nine cases separate absent, neutral, repeated neutral, tiny positive/negative,
and 25% brightness effects. Sixteen patches include alpha 0, 64, 128 and 255.

The reference application opened the exact source read-only and exported
`native.pdf`. The page was visually inspected. The recorder keeps PDF image bytes,
soft-mask alpha/Matte, and composited page RGB distinct. `reference.json`
binds the observations to source, case and PDF SHA-256 hashes.

For source RGBA(200,40,80,128), the absent effect and one, two or three neutral
effects all store image RGB(100,20,40) with mask 128. Brightness +1/100000 stores
(99,19,39); -1/100000 stores (98,18,38). Brightness +25000/100000 stores
(128,50,70). Mask alpha remains 128 throughout. This identifies a precision
change on entering a nonzero effect path, which neutral effects bypass. It does
not establish a general transfer function for every alpha value or prove that
PDF compositing rounding is identical to the reference application's screen rendering.

ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.1.8.42 defines brightness/contrast and preservation of alpha,
but does not specify the exact channel quantization. These native observations
constrain the unresolved semitransparent luminance implementation; the existing
opaque formula must not be changed merely to fit these two partial-alpha levels.
The provenance tests are evidence integrity checks, not renderer conformance.
No production change or resolution of the existing expected failure is claimed.

## Native display is a separate reference

`word-display-{upper,middle,lower}.jpg` capture this exact control in the reference application at 100% zoom, without editing. `native-display-reference.json` records their
hashes, pixel sample coordinates and the current browser's composited colors.
The captures are JPEG, so their sampled values MUST NOT be used as byte-exact
rendering expectations. They distinguish the application display from the PDF
export path. In the +25% case, the alpha-128 patch is (254,179,199) in the
capture, (255,179,199) in the browser and (255,176,196) in the PDF page reference.
The gray-64 opaque patch is (128,128,128) in the capture but (127,127,127) in the
PDF and browser. Native display and export have different rounding behavior;
matching the PDF's stored premultiplied samples is insufficient proof of an
on-screen rendering correction. A lossless display reference is needed before
changing the low-amplitude channel rounding. The browser expected failure
continues to assert the same exact PDF color, labeled as an export comparison.
